root_idea.summary: The root centers on roughness, thickness, and coarseness.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends from rugged mountains, hard or stony ground, and coarse-bodied animals to roughly fashioned or unfinished objects, wood and timber, dry branches, unrefined speech, and austere living. The lexical record also preserves several specialized and divergent branches under particular derived forms.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized collective-noun citation form خَشَبٌ rather than the Quranic plural surface form خُشُبٌ.

senses.definition: Wood or timber; pieces of wood.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural خُشُبٌ occurs in كَأَنَّهُمْ خُشُبٌ مُسَنَّدَةٌ (63:4), using propped-up timbers as a simile for the hypocrites because of their lack of usefulness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mix one thing with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The mixed object is construed with باء.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pick out, choose, or select something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is recorded as a contrasting branch of the verb’s meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To polish or sharpen a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The operation involves rubbing the sword with a broad, smooth implement; the basic reference is to sword finishing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To forge or roughly fashion a sword, arrow, or bow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be shaped by the initial filing or forging operation without being fully smoothed, perfected, or evenly finished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To speak, compose, or perform without refinement or careful preparation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of poetry, words, or work produced as it comes, without studied elegance or thoroughness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To eat thick branches or dry herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of camels taking and eating branches of trees or other dry vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or adopt a sword without selecting the best one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes taking a sword from one place or another indiscriminately.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become tall, gross, rough, coarse, and hard-bodied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, camel, or ostrich, with emphasis on a coarse or hardy physical condition and, for a person or camel, prominent bones or lack of flesh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become rough or austere in one’s way of life and outward conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The recorded figurative application extends to religion, clothing, food, and conduct generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To undertake or endure a hard life in order to become more able to bear hardship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage includes subjecting oneself to arduous work or barefoot walking to toughen the body, and patiently enduring difficult living conditions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Worthless or lacking any good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression رَجُلٌ قِشْبٌ خِشْبٌ, describing a man in whom or with whom there is no good; the form is also described as an imitative sequent to قِشْبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lean or emaciated cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application attributed to cattle made lean by feeding on dry herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rough, coarse, gross, hard, or tough-bodied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people and animals, including a large or coarse camel, a thick-boned horse, or a body with prominent bones and sinews; the description can also mean dry, rigid, or vigorous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A life lacking delicacy, nicety, or scrupulousness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative description of austere or rough living.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first filing of a sword before polishing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical term for the sword’s initial finishing stage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beverage properly called نَبِيذٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry identifies this word as deriving from Persian خُوشْ آبْ; it is a homonymous borrowed lexical item.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mixed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied lexical statement is terse and does not specify the construction or things mixed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Picked out, chosen, or selected.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is recorded as one of two contrasting applications of the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A polished or sharpened sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is especially reported for a sword that has been polished or sharpened.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A newly made, roughly forged, or unfinished sword, arrow, or bow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object has undergone initial forging or filing but has not yet been polished, smoothed, or fully perfected.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unpolished, unstudied speech or poetry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used figuratively of words uttered as they come, without refinement or labor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bad, corrupt, or vile.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general evaluative application of the adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The raw or unfinished quality of a sword’s metal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also be applied, according to the reported lexical alternatives, to the sword’s blade, iron, edge, or polish.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collective term for sellers of wood or timber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry treats the word as a collective designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fighters armed with staves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized plural or collective application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slender implement passed over a sword after polishing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The tool is used so that the scabbard does not alter its condition after the sword has been polished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great rugged mountain or a rugged, stony tract of elevated ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is also used of rugged mountains, rocky terrain, and ground of a rough, stony character.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard, stony ground containing stones, pebbles, and earth or clay.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ground is described as shedding or carrying off even a small amount of rain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hill whose stones are scattered but lie near one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction أَكَمَةٌ خَشْبَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Displeasing, rigid, or uneven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a forehead in جَبْهَةٌ خَشْبَاءُ and of a person described as أَخْشَبُ الجَبْهَةِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Built or furnished with wood or timber.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a house having wood employed in its construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse of mixed pedigree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized application attributed to a particular poetic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unbroken or poorly trained horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This application is reported as restricted to a particular poet’s usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Imperfectly made of wood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a wooden bowl that has been made roughly or inadequately.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Imperfectly prepared food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Meat may be undercooked; grain or other food may lack seasoning or condiment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who eats whatever he can obtain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A description of a person’s opportunistic eating.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The wood/timber meaning is covered by the Quranic noun sense.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is the plural خُشُبٌ; the public headword is normalized to the collective noun خَشَبٌ.
Some derived forms preserve contrasting lexical branches, such as mixing versus selecting and polished versus roughly forged; these have been kept distinct by headword and meaning.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Lane statement in lane-unit:x$b:19150:g1:main is supplied only as the terse gloss “Mixed”; the lexical meaning is represented under خَشِيبٌ, but its fuller construction is not recoverable from the packet.
